Amazon said it needs to locate its new headquarters in an area where there already is a workforce with strong technical skills. that the local-food movement was generating about $1 billion for the state economy.
So far this year, farmers who rely on direct-marketing have sold at least $96 million worth of locally grown foods, according to U.S. Department of Agriculture data that were recently reviewed by The Tennessean. Last year, that figure was $106 million.
Based on those figures, Tennessee farmers are cashing in on the local-food movement as it has grown in popularity across the nation. The movement has created opportunities for people to buy healthy foods and for producers to sell directly to consumers. A growing number of farmers markets have also opened throughout the state.

original:
10-foot high block walls with exposed rebar sit behind a chain link fence as an ugly reminder of how quickly the oceanfront condominium market crashed here in 2008.
But across from the site of the old Amory Condominiums on the Intracoastal Waterway, the $13 million development site is beginning to turn into a new luxury condo community — just in time for the holiday shopping season.
"It's kind of a pain to drive by," said Jim Spence, president of the New Smyrna Beach Boardwalk's management group, which is overseeing the redevelopment. "Hopefully when this project is done, people will look at it and say, 'Oh, that was one of the first condos I lived in.' It will just become part of the story."
The site of the Amory Condominiums on New Smyrna Beach's east side was cleared last year after its owners, Miami-based Minto Communities, went bankrupt in May 2012.

breaking temperatures in late 2016 and early 2017 caused the third consecutive event of coral bleaching in less than five years for the 2,300 mile-long (3,800km) reef, the world's largest and most extensive coral system.

"The latest forecasts indicate that the 2017 mass bleaching will be on a par with 2016's record bleaching and likely to be as severe as last year," said Terry Hughes, director of the ARC Centre of Excellence for Coral Reef Studies in Australia.

"While we are not surprised by this result, it nevertheless represents a monumental environmental crisis."

"Even for this resilient species, back-to-back bleaching events have devastated large areas of the reef," said Mark Eakin, coordinator of the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Coral Reef Watch Program.

"Unprecedented mortality will persist into next year in affected areas where coral mortality is likely to occur very quickly if heat stress is not mitigated."

the road and ploughed into a field on May 28 last year.

The engine failed on the drive across the A73 near the town of Stranraer, where he panicked and tried to get it working by turning the key in the ignition.
Simpson then tried to drive on, but the car rolled backwards before crashing into a field where it remained lodged.
Because Simpson had been drinking, police found him passed out in the driver's seat when they arrived and were unable to wake him.

Sheriff Colin Pettigrew decided that jail was too harsh a sanction given Simpson's "difficult" life as a former coal miner

able to obtain a much lower interest rate than we had been able to obtain through the first mortgage broker we tried.
The local bank has given us an acceptable disclosure form, which contains several statements and clauses not found in the contract. The most egregious, among others, is a provision that allows the lender to obtain a third-party opinion of our income-to-debt ratio at any time, even after the mortgage is consummated. The mortgage broker had also given us this same "loan to income" disclosure, which we had to submit to obtain a mortgage.
Given that the lender has no power to obtain a third-party opinion of our income-to-debt ratio, what is the purpose of this clause?
R.G.
DEAR R.G.: The purpose is to make it more difficult for an borrower to refinance in the future and keep the interest rate on your mortgage from rising.

company. I prefer my Thanksgiving dinner to be leisurely, not hurried. I'm convinced that if you plan well ahead of time, you can't beat a slow-cooked Thanksgiving dinner.

So I'm going to share my favorites for slow-cooking, here's hoping you enjoy a delicious and plentiful Thanksgiving.

Get a head start on your Thanksgiving dinner by making the mashed potatoes ahead of time. I always make my mashed potatoes with home-grown potatoes, because it takes a lot longer to cook them otherwise. The result is tender potatoes that don't need as much butter and cream to make creamier than usual.

Heat oil in a 5-6 quart Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onions and saute until soft, stirring constantly. Add garlic and saute another minute.

Add chopped turkey and saute about 10 minutes more or until browned. Season with salt and pepper.

Add potatoes, 1 cup water, 1/2 cup stock
